HOW I BUILD

Workflow before framework.

I choose tools after the problem is clear. The method stays steady even when the stack changes.

01 / TRACE

Follow the work as it happens now.

Who records what? Where does information get lost? What decision is delayed because the right person cannot see it?

OUTPUT → A workflow worth fixing
02 / SHAPE

Turn responsibilities into a product structure.

Roles, actions, states and data become a clear interface—not a collection of features competing for attention.

OUTPUT → A system people can understand
03 / SHIP

Build the smallest complete experience.

Frontend, backend, database and deployment come together around one usable flow, then improve through real feedback.

OUTPUT → Working software, not a slide

CURRENT CHAPTER / IUIU KC

Still a student.
Already shipping.

I’m completing my Bachelor of Science in Computer Science at the Islamic University in Uganda, Kampala Campus.

University gives me the foundations. Building products gives those foundations consequences: a schema must hold real records, a permission rule must protect the right person, and an interface must make sense without explanation.

I’m looking for the next environment where I can contribute, learn from experienced developers and keep turning practical problems into dependable software.
